questions.question: Explain why corrugated board is used for packaging rather than solid cardboard of the same weight.

points.text: Corrugated board's fluted structure creates air gaps between liners - this gives excellent compressive strength and cushioning while remaining lightweight. Solid cardboard of the same weight would be thinner and offer no cushioning.

questions.question: A designer needs to create a 3D architectural model. Justify the choice of foam-core board over corrugated board.

points.text: Foam-core: very smooth surface, extremely rigid for its weight, cuts cleanly with a craft knife, accepts pins. Corrugated board: visible fluting on edges, less refined. For architectural models, foam-core's clean finish and rigidity make it superior.

questions.question: Compare the suitability of cartridge paper and layout paper for producing a final design presentation.

points.text: Cartridge paper (120-300 gsm): thick enough to stand alone, textured surface holds ink well, professional. Layout paper (50-60 gsm): thin, semi-transparent - for rough layout work, not final output.
